_format: skill-creator evals.json plus evergreen fields (kind, decoy, evidence, baseline); extra fields are ignored by skill-creator's runner. Rules: the evergreen plugin's protocol/TESTING.md. Gold answers: RESEARCH.md R-20261017-12.

evals.prompt: When was Julius Caesar born? I want the real answer with sources, not a guess.
expectations: the historywright skill is invoked

evals.prompt: who was the longest ruling emperor in chinese history
expectations: the historywright skill is invoked

evals.prompt: When did Bill Gates found Microsoft, and who with?
expectations: the historywright skill is invoked

evals.prompt: What open archives or databases cover medieval Japan that I could actually query from a script?
expectations: the historywright-sources skill is invoked (historywright is acceptable family routing)

evals.prompt: I'm modelling a Roman legionary from around 50 BC for a 3D print. Research what he wore and collect period-accurate museum references I can model from.
expectations: the historywright-pack skill is invoked (historywright or polywright first is acceptable if historywright-pack follows)

evals.prompt: Write a short story set in ancient Rome about a gladiator who wants to retire.
expectations: no historywright skill is invoked (creative writing, not a factual question)

evals.prompt: Summarise this history PDF for me chapter by chapter: ./notes/rome-lectures.pdf
expectations: no historywright skill is invoked (reading a document is readwright's job)

evals.prompt: What happened in today's news about the elections?
expectations: no historywright skill is invoked (current news, not history)
before the final answer, the trace shows Wikidata's full statements read: hw.py wd claims, wbgetclaims, or a p:/psv: SPARQL query; a lone wdt:P569 query does not count

evals.prompt: When was Julius Caesar born? Save the researched answer so you don't have to look it up again.
expectations: the trace shows hw.py cache put writing the entry (under claude plugin eval in WSL2, also check $HW_HOME/cache/*.json has question, answer and sources with url and retrieved)

evals.prompt: Check the two research packs in tests/fixtures/pack-good and tests/fixtures/pack-bad and tell me which one is valid and what is wrong with the other.
expectations: the trace shows hw.py validate-pack run on both folders
says pack-good passes and pack-bad fails, naming at least three of its problems
regex on the answer: pack-good.{0,200}(pass|valid)
regex on the answer: pack-bad.{0,300}(fail|invalid|not valid)
gives 12 or 13 July 100 BC (both days, or the date range), not one day stated as certain
attributes the days: 12 July to Macrobius or the official festival, 13 July to Cassius Dio or a disputed reading
notes that some scholars (Mommsen) argued for 102 BC and that 100 BC is the consensus
cites at least two sources and has a confidence line
regex on the answer: (12|twelfth).{0,40}(13|thirteenth).{0,15}July|July (12|12th).{0,25}(13|13th)
regex on the answer: 100 BC|100 BCE|100 B\.C
regex on the answer: Mommsen|102 BC
regex on the answer: ^(?!.*\b99 BCE?\b)(?!.*\b11 July)(?!.*July 11\b)

evals.prompt: Who was the longest-ruling emperor in Chinese history?
expectations: names the Kangxi Emperor with a formal reign of 61 years, 1661 to 1722
adds that Qianlong abdicated in 1796 but held power until his death in 1799, the longest de facto rule
classifies the difference as a frame (formal reign against actual power), not an error
regex on the answer: Kangxi
regex on the answer: 61 years|sixty-one years
regex on the answer: 1661
regex on the answer: 1722
regex on the answer: Qianlong
regex on the answer: 1799

evals.prompt: When did Bill Gates found Microsoft, and with whom?
expectations: Bill Gates and Paul Allen, 4 April 1975 (April 4, 1975), in Albuquerque, New Mexico
does not claim that an official Microsoft page states the day; may note the 1981 incorporation
cites sources it fetched
regex on the answer: Allen
regex on the answer: April 4,? 1975|4 April,? 1975
regex on the answer: Albuquerque

evals.prompt: What date did the October Revolution happen?
expectations: gives 25 October 1917 Old Style (Julian) and 7 November 1917 New Style (Gregorian), and says why both exist
the conversion is computed (hw.py cal) or quoted from a fetched source, not asserted from memory
regex on the answer: 25 October|October 25
regex on the answer: 7 November|November 7
regex on the answer: Julian|Old Style|O\.S\.

evals.prompt: How long did Emperor Menelik II rule Ethiopia?
expectations: gives his reign as emperor from 1889 to his death in 1913 (about 24 years) with sources
notes the frame: strokes left him incapacitated in his last years, with others governing (a regency) before 1913
the confidence line or note reflects thinner sources for the region, or cites a regional or scholarly source
regex on the answer: 1889
regex on the answer: 1913
regex on the answer: stroke|incapacit|regen

evals.prompt: Name five key books on the Haitian Revolution, and check that each one really exists.
expectations: lists five books with author and year
the trace shows each checked in a catalogue or index (OpenAlex, Crossref, Open Library, a library catalogue, WorldCat or a publisher page), not only recalled
no invented title: every listed book matches a fetched catalogue record on title, author and year
regex on the answer: (?:.*?\b(?:19|20)\d\d\b){5}

evals.prompt: Did Marie Antoinette really say 'Let them eat cake'?
expectations: says there is no evidence she said it; the line appears in Rousseau's Confessions about an unnamed great princess, written when she was a child
cites a fetched source for that, and does not present the quote as hers
regex on the answer: Rousseau
regex on the answer: no (reliable |contemporary |historical )?(evidence|record|source)|never said|misattribut|apocryphal|did not say|didn't say

evals.prompt: Several websites say the electric toaster was invented by Alan MacMasters in 1893. Is that right?
expectations: says the MacMasters claim was a Wikipedia hoax that spread to other sites (citogenesis), so the agreeing websites are not independent confirmation
does not confirm MacMasters as the inventor
regex on the answer: hoax
regex on the answer: not (the )?(real |actual )?inventor|no evidence|fabricat|invented by a|made up|false
